Usage: mail-find <command> [flags]

mail-find searches, reads and downloads from mail history. Nothing here sends or changes mail.

Reads the person's mail: find a message, read it, reassemble its
conversation or everything about the same order, booking or tenancy, and
download what is attached. Every command prints one JSON document; --text
prints the form for people instead.

An ID is the "id" field that search, resolve and thread print, and it
belongs to the account it came from. A Message-ID (the RFC 822 header, or a
message:// link dragged out of a mail client) is not an ID: resolve turns
one into an ID.

search, read, context and attachments results carry next_steps: runnable
commands for what the tool saw but did not do, such as pictures it did not
fetch, the conversation a message belongs to, or matches it held back. Run
the ones that bear on the question.

An error that says the account is not authenticated names the command that
signs it in again. Signing in needs the person at the keyboard: relay the
command to them rather than running it.

Flags:
  -h, --help               Show context-sensitive help.
      --account=ACCOUNT    Which account's mailbox to read. An id from one account means nothing in
                           the other (default: gmail; one of: gmail, outlook).
      --text               Print the human form instead of one JSON document.

Commands:
  search <query>      Find messages by sender, recipient, subject, date or phrase.
  resolve <ref>       Turn a Message-ID, or a message:// link from a mail client, into the message's
                      id.
  read <id>           Print one message: headers, the body with verified quoted history folded, and
                      its attachments.
  thread <id>         Print the conversation a message belongs to as one transcript, each turn
                      saying only what it added.
  context <id>        Find messages about the same real-world thing across threads and senders; each
                      hit says why.
  attachments <id>    List a message's attachments and the pictures its body only links to.
  fetch (--attachment=NAME | --all) <id>
                      Download a message's attachments and print where each landed.
  auth login          Sign in to --account interactively: a browser for Gmail, a device code for
                      Outlook.
  auth status         Print the address --account is signed in as, and the largest message it can
                      send.

Examples:
  mail-find search 'from:taskrabbit.co.uk newer_than:30d'
  mail-find read 1a02340ea531858a
  mail-find thread 1a02340ea531858a
  mail-find context 1a02367a18eae254

Exit codes:
  0    success
  1    failed
  2    invalid arguments; nothing was run

Run "mail-find <command> --help" for a command's details.
